chain: RBI is India's central bank — it controls how much it costs for banks to borrow money
REPO RATE = the interest rate RBI charges when banks borrow from it
When RBI HOLDS the rate → banks' borrowing costs STAY THE SAME
Same cost for banks → they don't increase loan EMIs for customers
No EMI increase → you keep spending on houses, cars, and goods
People spending → companies earn more profits → stock prices go UP 📈

sectors.Banking: ⭐ Direct: stable NIMs benefit HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, SBI
sectors.Auto: ✅ Positive: stable loan EMIs means car buying continues
sectors.Real Estate: ✅ Positive: home loan rates unchanged, supports buying

chain: RBI is India's central bank
When RBI CUTS the REPO RATE → it becomes CHEAPER for banks to borrow
Lower cost for banks → they reduce loan interest rates for customers
Cheaper EMIs → you borrow more for houses, cars, and businesses
More borrowing → more spending → more profits for companies
Companies grow → stock market goes UP 📈

sectors.Banking: ⭐ Direct: lower cost of funds, positive for all banks
sectors.Auto: ✅ Strong: cheaper car loans drive sales
sectors.Real Estate: ✅ Strong: lower home loan rates boost demand
sectors.NBFCs: ✅ Positive: lower borrowing costs improve margins

chain: RBI is India's central bank
When RBI HIKES the REPO RATE → it becomes MORE EXPENSIVE for banks to borrow
Higher cost for banks → they increase loan interest rates for customers
More expensive EMIs → you borrow less for houses, cars, and businesses
Less borrowing → less spending → companies earn less profit
Company profits fall → stock market goes DOWN 📉

sectors.Banking: ⭐ Direct: may benefit from higher NIMs but loan growth slows
sectors.Auto: 🔴 Negative: expensive car loans reduce demand
sectors.Real Estate: 🔴 Negative: high home loan rates reduce buying

chain: The US Federal Reserve is America's central bank — like RBI for the USA
When US Fed CUTS rates → money becomes CHEAPER in the US
Cheaper money in US → investors look for higher returns in other countries
Foreign investors put money into Indian stock market (FII inflows)
More money flowing into India → Nifty goes UP 📈

sectors.IT: ⭐ Direct: weaker USD means higher revenue for Indian IT exports
sectors.Banking: ✅ Positive: FII inflows boost banking stocks

chain: US Federal Reserve kept rates unchanged — no change in global money flows
Markets already expected this decision, so no major impact expected
Focus shifts to Fed's future guidance for the next signal
US Federal Reserve HIKED rates → money becomes MORE EXPENSIVE in the US
US investors keep money in US (higher returns available there)
Foreign investors SELL Indian stocks and take money back to US (FII outflows)
FII selling → Nifty goes DOWN 📉

sectors.IT: ⭐ Direct: stronger USD was helping but rate hikes slow global economy

chain: CPI = Consumer Price Index — it measures how much prices of everyday things have gone up
When CPI comes ABOVE expectations → prices rose more than expected
Higher inflation → people's money buys less → they spend less
RBI also worries about high inflation → may KEEP rates high
Both effects combined → negative for stock market 📉

sectors.Banking: ⚠️ Mixed: high inflation may delay RBI rate cuts
sectors.Consumer Goods: 🔴 Negative: people buy less when prices are high
sectors.FMCG: 🔴 Negative: input costs rise, demand falls

chain: CPI = Consumer Price Index — measures price rise of everyday things
When CPI comes BELOW expectations → prices rose less than expected
Lower inflation → RBI has room to CUT rates in future
Rate cuts expected → banks may lower EMIs → you spend more
More spending → company profits rise → stock market UP 📈

sectors.Banking: ✅ Positive: rate cut hopes increase, positive for all banks
sectors.Auto: ✅ Positive: cheaper loans expected in future

chain: Union Budget = Government's annual spending plan for the country
When government focuses on CAPEX (building roads, railways, bridges)
Construction companies get big contracts → they hire more workers
Workers earn money → they spend on goods → economy grows
Infrastructure + consumption growth → stock market UP 📈

sectors.Infrastructure: ⭐ Direct: L&T, HCC get major contracts
sectors.Cement: ✅ Positive: more construction needs more cement
sectors.Capital Goods: ✅ Positive: increased government spending boosts orders

chain: Union Budget = Government's spending plan
When budget focuses on FARMERS and POOR (free schemes, subsidies)
Rural demand gets a boost → people in villages spend more
FMCG companies, tractor makers, and two-wheeler companies benefit
Rural India consuming more → select stocks go UP 📈

sectors.Auto (2-wheelers): ✅ Positive: higher rural income → more purchases

chain: Union Budget = Government's spending plan
Government focuses on reducing DEFICIT (spending less than it earns)
Lower deficit → RBI happy → bond yields fall → interest rates may come down
Rate cuts → cheaper loans → economy grows → stock market UP 📈

sectors.Banking: ✅ Positive: falling bond yields = banks' bond profits rise
sectors.Bonds: ✅ Positive: bond prices rise as yields fall

chain: GDP = Gross Domestic Product — measures how fast the Indian economy is growing
When GDP comes ABOVE expectations → economy is growing faster than thought
Fast growth → companies sell more → they earn more profits
Foreign investors also get attracted to a fast-growing India
FII inflows + strong earnings → stock market UP 📈

sectors.Banking: ✅ Positive: fast growth = more loans = bank profits rise
sectors.All: ✅ Broad positive impact across all sectors

chain: GDP = Gross Domestic Product — measures Indian economy's growth speed
When GDP comes BELOW expectations → economy is slowing down
Slow growth → companies sell less → they earn less profit
RBI may need to cut rates → but only if inflation is low
Until then, market remains NEGATIVE 📉

sectors.Banking: 🔴 Negative: slow growth = fewer loans = bank profits fall

chain: Earnings season = companies report their quarterly profits
When a company BEATS estimates → its profit is HIGHER than expected
Higher profits → company has more money → can give dividends, invest more
Investors get excited → buy more shares → stock price goes UP 📈
Earnings season = companies report their quarterly profits
When a company MISSES estimates → its profit is LOWER than expected
Lower profits → company struggles → may cut costs or jobs
Investors get worried → sell shares → stock price goes DOWN 📉
Global markets (US, Europe, Asia) affect Indian markets too
When global markets SELL-OFF (crash) → investors worldwide get scared
Foreign investors sell Indian stocks to cover losses elsewhere
Even strong Indian companies get sold in panic → Nifty DOWN 📉
This is usually temporary — markets recover in a few days

sectors.IT: 🔴 Negative: most exposed to global economy

chain: Geopolitical tensions (war, conflict) create uncertainty in markets
War → oil prices may rise → India (oil importer) gets hurt
Uncertainty → companies delay investments → economy slows
Risk-off mood → investors sell stocks → market DOWN 📉

sectors.Oil & Gas: 🔴 Negative: higher crude oil costs hurt OMCs

chain: India imports most of its oil — when crude prices SPIKE, it hurts
Higher oil price → India pays more for the same oil
More money going out → rupee becomes weaker vs dollar
Oil companies, airlines get hurt → their costs rise
Inflation may also rise → RBI can't cut rates → market DOWN 📉

sectors.Oil Marketing: 🔴 Negative: buy oil at high price, forced to sell at government-fixed rates
sectors.Aviation: 🔴 Negative: jet fuel is their biggest cost
